name: Forest Road 525 Dispersed Camping Area - Coconino National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Red Rock Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Designated dispersed camping corridor (no fees)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Camping permitted ONLY in designated marked campsites along FR 525 corridor. Vehicles must park within campsite boundaries. No camping within 1 mile of State Route 89A.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Extreme dry high-desert soil: cat-holes must be 6 inches deep, at least 200ft from washes and campsites. Packing out toilet paper in sealed bags is strictly required.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Leave No Trace strictly enforced. No trash dumpsters on site; all waste must be hauled out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Dead and down wood gathering permitted. Do not break branches off live mesquite, juniper, or pinon pine.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires permitted only in existing stone/metal fire rings when fire restrictions allow. Douse fire completely with water until cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Stage 1 and Stage 2 fire restrictions strictly implemented in early summer (May-July) before monsoon season.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved dirt and washboard gravel forest road (FR 525)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Heavy washboards and dust during dry season; red clay slickness and rutting after heavy rains/monsoons.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible at slow speeds on main FR 525 corridor; high clearance recommended for side spurs)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low to Moderate (open high desert mesa with red rock bluffs in background)

amenities: Panoramic Red Rock & Mingus Mountain Views

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 65-80°F pleasant days, breezy wind gusts (20-30 mph), excellent camping weather.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot 95-105°F early summer; July-August monsoon season brings dramatic afternoon thunderstorms, flash floods, and red mud.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal boondocking season (70-85°F), clear sunny skies, cool comfortable nights (45-55°F).
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool crisp days (50-60°F), freezing night temperatures (25-35°F), rare dustings of snow on surrounding red rock peaks.

dangers_and_hazards: Western Diamondback Rattlesnakes and Black-tailed Rattlesnakes active in warm months
Flash flooding in dry washes during summer monsoons
Dehydration and heat exhaustion during peak summer
OHV / Jeep tour dust and traffic during busy weekends

acoustic_environment.quietness_rating: 7/10 - Quiet at night; daytime tour traffic noise
common_human_made_sounds: Pink Jeep tours and side-by-side OHV engines during daytime
Distant scenic flight helicopters or small propeller aircraft overhead

human_demographics_and_culture: Full-time digital nomads, vanlifers, mountain bikers, OHV enthusiasts, spiritual seekers visiting Sedona vortexes, and RV boondockers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Yavapai-Apache sacred creation lore centers on nearby Boynton Canyon ('Palatkwapi') and the Red Rocks as spiritual emergence lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Proximity to world-famous Sedona energy vortexes (Boynton Canyon, Bell Rock, Airport Mesa). High electromagnetic earth energy, renowned for inspiring clarity, deep dream activity, and spiritual grounding.

Hidden arch, canyon walls, lush high-desert vegetation

public_reviews_summary: Extremely popular nomad hotspot due to killer 5G cell speeds and stunning red rock vistas. Can get busy on weekends, so arrive early in the week to secure prime designated spots.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. High solar panel efficiency due to 300+ annual days of sunshine.

name: Kofa National Wildlife Refuge Dispersed Primitive Camping (Palm Canyon Road)

management_agency.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Kofa National Wildlife Refuge

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No permits or fees required for primitive camping
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted within 100 feet of established public access roads. Camping prohibited within 1/4 mile of artificial water holes or natural guzzlers.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Strict desert pack-out or deep cat-hole (6 inches deep in sandy washes, 200ft from drainages). Pack out all toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Zero trash services on refuge. All waste and food scraps must be packed out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood. Gathering of desert ironwood, palo verde, or saguaro rib wood is strictly illegal on wildlife refuge lands.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Use containerized fire pans or existing rock rings. Extinguish with water until cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Enforced during hot summer fire season.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved desert dirt and gravel road (Palm Canyon Road / Queen Canyon Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboarded gravel main road; secondary spurs have sharp volcanic rocks, dip washes, and loose sand pockets.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance car or 4x4 (Normal low clearance 2WD cars can reach lower Palm Canyon Road pullouts if driven very carefully, but high clearance recommended)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Jagged Kofa Mountains create signal shadows near mountain base)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 75-85°F ideal conditions, blooming desert wildflowers and ocotillo.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Extremely hot (105-118°F), dangerous life-threatening heat, boondocking NOT recommended.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Warm pleasant days (80-90°F), cool starry nights (55-65°F).
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Premier winter desert haven (65-75°F daytime, 40-50°F night).
